chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Humayri narrated to us, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mus'ada ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, peace be upon them,

Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) said: 'For a Muslim man there are three friends. A friend who says: I am with you alive and dead, and that is his deeds. A friend who says to him: I am with you until the door of your grave, then I leave you, and that is his child. A friend who says to him: I am with you until you die, and that is his wealth. So when he dies, it becomes for the inheritor.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three friends of a Muslim according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Khisal, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) delineates the transient nature of worldly attachments by contrasting the permanence of one's deeds with the limited companionship of offspring and wealth. This tripartite classification underscores the Shia emphasis on 'amal (action) as the sole enduring legacy that accompanies the soul beyond the grave, while children and wealth remain bound to the material realm and its inheritance laws.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-92 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Abdullah ibn Ja’far al-Homayry quoted Harun ibn Muslim, on the authority of Mus’adat ibn Zyad, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his father Al-Baqir (MGB), on the authority of his grandfather (MGB) that Ali (MGB) said, “There are three friends for a Muslim. There is a friend who says, ‘I will be with you in your life and death!’ That is his deeds! There is a friend who says, ‘I will be with you until you are put into the grave. Then I will abandon you.’ That is his child! There is a friend who says, ‘I will be with you until your death.’ That is his wealth which will be that of his inheritors once he dies.’”
